claim: Arp2/3 complex activation by nucleation promoting factors (NPFs) such as WASP plays an important role in many actin-mediated cellular processes.
source: Actin-related protein 2/3 (Arp2/3) complex activation by nucleation promoting factors (NPFs) such as WASP, plays an important role in many actin-mediated cellular processes.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by established scientific knowledge in the field of cell biology.

claim: In yeast, Arp2/3-mediated actin filament assembly drives endocytic membrane invagination and vesicle scission.
source: In yeast, Arp2/3-mediated actin filament assembly drives endocytic membrane invagination and vesicle scission.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge and is presented as background information.

claim: SH3 domain-PRM interactions involving multivalent linker proteins play central roles in concentrating NPFs at endocytic sites.
source: Our results demonstrate that SH3 (Src homology 3) domain-PRM (proline-rich motif) interactions involving multivalent linker proteins play central roles in concentrating NPFs at endocytic sites.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Productive actin assembly initiation is tightly coupled to accumulation of threshold levels of WASP and WIP.
source: Quantitative imaging suggested that productive actin assembly initiation is tightly coupled to accumulation of threshold levels of WASP and WIP, but not to recruitment kinetics or release of autoinhibition.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Productive actin assembly initiation is not coupled to recruitment kinetics of WASP and WIP.
source: Quantitative imaging suggested that productive actin assembly initiation is tightly coupled to accumulation of threshold levels of WASP and WIP, but not to recruitment kinetics or release of autoinhibition.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Productive actin assembly initiation is not coupled to release of autoinhibition of WASP and WIP.
source: Quantitative imaging suggested that productive actin assembly initiation is tightly coupled to accumulation of threshold levels of WASP and WIP, but not to recruitment kinetics or release of autoinhibition.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: WASP and WIP play central roles in establishment of a robust multivalent SH3 domain-PRM network in vivo.
source: These studies provide evidence that WASP and WIP play central roles in establishment of a robust multivalent SH3 domain-PRM network in vivo, giving actin assembly onset at endocytic sites a switch-like behavior.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental data.

claim: Actin assembly onset at endocytic sites has a switch-like behavior.
source: These studies provide evidence that WASP and WIP play central roles in establishment of a robust multivalent SH3 domain-PRM network in vivo, giving actin assembly onset at endocytic sites a switch-like behavior.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on experimental data.

claim: NPFs often contain additional functional elements that mediate interactions with other proteins.
source: In addition to VCA motifs (composed of a Verprolin homology domain, Central hydrophobic region, and Acidic region) that directly stimulate Arp2/3 complex-mediated actin nucleation, NPFs often contain additional functional elements that mediate interactions with other proteins (Padrick and Rosen, 2010; Takenawa and Suetsugu, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The EVH1 domain of N-WASP interacts with WIP.
source: For example, the EVH1 domain (Ena/VASP homology) of N-WASP (Neural Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome protein) interacts with WIP (WASP-interacting protein) (Donnelly et al., 2013; Rivera et al., 2004; Tehrani et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Most WASP family proteins contain a large proline-rich domain (PRD) that contains multiple Src homology 3 (SH3)-binding proline-rich motifs (PRMs).
source: In addition, most WASP family proteins, which are the best-studied NPFs, also contain a large proline-rich domain (PRD) that contains multiple Src homology 3 (SH3)-binding proline-rich motifs (PRMs).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about WASP family protein structure.

claim: Dozens of SH3-domain containing ligands can bind to WASP PRMs.
source: Previous studies demonstrated that dozens of SH3-domain containing ligands can bind to WASP PRMs, and that some enhance WASP NPF activity (Donnelly et al., 2013; Padrick and Rosen, 2010; Rivera et al., 2004; Tehrani et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Some SH3-domain containing ligands enhance WASP NPF activity.
source: Previous studies demonstrated that dozens of SH3-domain containing ligands can bind to WASP PRMs, and that some enhance WASP NPF activity (Donnelly et al., 2013; Padrick and Rosen, 2010; Rivera et al., 2004; Tehrani et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Multivalent PRM-SH3 domain interactions between N-WASP and its ligands enable proteins to form higher order complexes in vitro on artificial membranes.
source: Multivalent PRM-SH3 domain interactions between N-WASP and its ligands enable proteins to form higher order complexes in vitro on artificial membranes and undergo a phase separation, producing micrometer-size clusters (Banjade and Rosen, 2014; Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Multivalent PRM-SH3 domain interactions between N-WASP and its ligands undergo a phase separation, producing micrometer-size clusters.
source: Multivalent PRM-SH3 domain interactions between N-WASP and its ligands enable proteins to form higher order complexes in vitro on artificial membranes and undergo a phase separation, producing micrometer-size clusters (Banjade and Rosen, 2014; Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: N-WASP and WIP clusters robustly trigger Arp2/3-mediated actin assembly.
source: Interestingly, such clusters robustly trigger Arp2/3-mediated actin assembly (Banjade and Rosen, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In budding yeast, all known NPFs and over 50 other proteins are organized into plasma membrane-associated patches, which are clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) sites.
source: In budding yeast, all known NPFs and over 50 other proteins are organized into plasma membrane-associated patches, which are clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) sites (Kaksonen et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Each endocytic protein is recruited to endocytic sites in a predictable order and with predictable timing.
source: In addition, a very detailed pathway has been elucidated in which each endocytic protein is recruited to endocytic sites in a predictable order and with predictable timing (Figure 1A)(Lu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The two most important NPFs in yeast are WASP (Las17) and type I myosin (Myo3 and Myo5).
source: The two most important NPFs, yeast WASP (Las17) and type I myosin (Myo3 and Myo5), which form a complex with yeast WIP (Vrp1) and additional binding partners, can be grouped into a WASP-Myosin module (Kaksonen et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The WASP-Myosin module stimulates actin filament assembly and provides motor activity, facilitating membrane invagination and vesicle scission.
source: The WASP-Myosin module stimulates actin filament assembly and provides motor activity, facilitating membrane invagination and vesicle scission (Galletta et al., 2008; Lewellyn et al., 2015; Sirotkin et al., 2005; Soulard et al., 2002; Sun et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Las17 appears first at endocytic sites, followed by Vrp1, and finally Myo3/5, coinciding with the onset of robust actin filament assembly.
source: Individual components of the WASP-Myosin module are recruited to endocytic sites in a regular, timely order, in which Las17 appears first, followed by Vrp1, and finally Myo3/5, coinciding with the onset of robust actin filament assembly (Sun et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: When Pan1 and End3 are eliminated from cells by an auxin-based degron method, endocytic sites still assemble at the cell cortex, but WASP-Myosin proteins associate with actin comet tails in the cytoplasm instead of with the endocytic sites.
source: When Pan1 and End3 are eliminated from cells by an auxin-based degron method, endocytic sites still assemble at the cell cortex, but WASP-Myosin proteins associate with actin comet tails in the cytoplasm instead of with the endocytic sites (Sun et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The Pan1-End3-Sla1 complex plays essential roles in coupling actin assembly to endocytic sites.
source: These findings indicate that the Pan1-End3-Sla1 complex plays essential roles in coupling actin assembly to endocytic sites.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the findings described in the previous sentence.

claim: sla1∆ displays a synthetic lethal interaction with pan1∆PRD.
source: Previous studies revealed a synthetic lethal interaction between sla1∆ and pan1∆PRD, in which the Pan1 C-terminal PRD (proline-rich domain) is truncated (Barker et al., 2007)(Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature and reference to a figure.

claim: The Pan1 PRD has been shown to interact with yeast type 1 myosin (Myo3 and Myo5) SH3 domain and enhance Myo3/5-Vrp1 NPF activity in vitro.
source: The Pan1 PRD has been shown to interact with yeast type 1 myosin (Myo3 and Myo5) SH3 domain and enhance Myo3/5-Vrp1 NPF activity in vitro (Barker et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: sla1∆ does not display a synthetic lethal interaction with myo5CA∆myo3∆.
source: However, sla1∆ does not display a synthetic lethal interaction with myo5CA∆myo3∆ (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), in which the type 1 myosin NPF activity is abolished (Sun et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to a figure and a citation to previous literature.

claim: pan1∆PRD does not appear to cause synthetic lethality with sla1∆ by affecting Myo3/5-Vrp1 NPF activity.
source: Thus, pan1∆PRD does not appear to cause synthetic lethality with sla1∆ by affecting Myo3/5-Vrp1 NPF activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of genetic interactions.

claim: Two amino acid substitutions in Sla1 (W41A and W108A) are sufficient to cause a synthetic genetic interaction with pan1∆PRD.
source: Strikingly, we found that two amino acid substitutions in Sla1 are sufficient to cause a synthetic genetic interaction with pan1∆PRD. sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells display severe growth defects at 25°C and 30°C, and are inviable at 37°C (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells display severe growth defects at 25°C and 30°C, and are inviable at 37°C.
source: sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells display severe growth defects at 25°C and 30°C, and are inviable at 37°C (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: W41 and W108 are the conserved tryptophan residues in two SH3 domains of Sla1.
source: W41 and W108 are the conserved tryptophan residues in two SH3 (SRC homology 3) domains of Sla1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) (Rodal et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by reference to a figure and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Point mutation of W41 and W108 abolishes the SH3 domain interactions with PRMs.
source: Point mutation of these sites abolishes the SH3 domain interactions with PRMs (Rodal et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A point mutation (W391A) on the third SH3 domain of Sla1 did not show a synthetic interaction with pan1∆PRD.
source: However, a point mutation (W391A) on the third SH3 domain of Sla1 did not show a synthetic interaction with pan1∆PRD (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The first two SH3 domains of Sla1 and the PRD of Pan1 function in parallel to provide a crucial role for cell growth.
source: Thus, our results indicate that the first two SH3 domains of Sla1 and the PRD of Pan1 function in parallel to provide a crucial role for cell growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic interaction data.

claim: sla1W41AW108A-GFP is well expressed.
source: Immunoblotting of whole cell extracts showed that sla1W41AW108A-GFP is well expressed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on immunoblotting data shown in the figure.

claim: sla1W41AW108A-GFP appeared in cortical patches that reached fluorescence intensity levels similar to wild-type Sla1-GFP patches.
source: More importantly, sla1W41AW108A-GFP appeared in cortical patches that reached fluorescence intensity levels similar to wild-type Sla1-GFP patches (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: The sla1W41AW108A-GFP patch lifetimes were substantially longer and more variable compared to Sla1-GFP patches (78.8 ± 31.2 vs 24.1 ± 4.9, p<0.0001).
source: However, the sla1W41AW108A-GFP patch lifetimes were substantially longer and more variable compared to Sla1-GFP patches (78.8 ± 31.2 vs 24.1 ± 4.9, p<0.0001) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: sla1W41AW108A-GFP patches moved inward, off the cell cortex, at the end of their lifetime.
source: Nevertheless, similar to the wild-type cells, sla1W41AW108A-GFP patches moved inward, off the cell cortex, at the end of their lifetime (Figure 1E), indicating that endocytic internalization still takes place in this mutant.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Endocytic internalization still takes place in sla1W41AW108A mutant.
source: Nevertheless, similar to the wild-type cells, sla1W41AW108A-GFP patches moved inward, off the cell cortex, at the end of their lifetime (Figure 1E), indicating that endocytic internalization still takes place in this mutant.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of patch movement.

claim: pan1∆PRD-GFP is expressed at levels similar to the wild-type protein.
source: Immunoblotting showed that pan1∆PRD-GFP is also expressed at levels similar to the wild-type protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on immunoblotting data shown in the figure.

claim: Cortical pan1∆PRD-GFP patches reached fluorescence intensity levels similar to wild-type Pan1-GFP patches.
source: In addition, cortical pan1∆PRD-GFP patches reached fluorescence intensity levels similar to wild-type Pan1-GFP patches (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: pan1∆PRD-GFP patch lifetimes were slightly shorter than Pan1-GFP lifetimes (23.6 ± 4.2 vs 28.5 ± 5.5, p<0.0001).
source: Finally, pan1∆PRD-GFP patch lifetimes were slightly shorter than Pan1-GFP lifetimes (23.6 ± 4.2 vs 28.5 ± 5.5, p<0.0001) (Figure 1G), and they were internalized at the end of their lifetime (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: pan1∆PRD-GFP patches were internalized at the end of their lifetime.
source: Finally, pan1∆PRD-GFP patch lifetimes were slightly shorter than Pan1-GFP lifetimes (23.6 ± 4.2 vs 28.5 ± 5.5, p<0.0001) (Figure 1G), and they were internalized at the end of their lifetime (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Neither a point mutant of two Sla1 SH3 domains nor a PRD truncation mutant of Pan1 affects either protein's expression or cortical recruitment.
source: The results described above establish that neither a point mutant of two Sla1 SH3 domains nor a PRD truncation mutant of Pan1 affects either protein's expression or cortical recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The severe synthetic growth defect of an sla1 W41AW108A pan1∆PRD double mutant is caused by the loss of specific functions rather than by the absence of the mutant proteins at endocytic sites.
source: Thus, the severe synthetic growth defect of an sla1 W41AW108A pan1∆PRD double mutant is caused by the loss of specific functions rather than by the absence of the mutant proteins at endocytic sites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Sla1 is recruited to endocytic sites by Pan1 and End3.
source: Previous studies suggested that Sla1 is recruited to endocytic sites by Pan1 and End3 (Sun et al., 2015; Tang et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sla1 (or the sla1 mutant) appears slightly after Pan1 (or the pan1 mutant), and then internalizes in wild-type cells, pan1∆PRD cells, and sla1W41AW108A cells.
source: Sla1 (or the sla1 mutant) appears slightly after Pan1 (or the pan1 mutant), and then internalizes in wild-type cells, pan1∆PRD cells, and sla1W41AW108A cells (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: Patch lifetimes in sla1W41AW108A cells are irregular and longer than in wild-type and pan1∆PRD cells.
source: Consistent with the results in Figure 1D, patch lifetimes in sla1W41AW108A cells are irregular and longer than in wild-type and pan1∆PRD cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: In the double mutants, sla1W41AW108A and pan1∆PRD colocalize as stable patches at the cell cortex.
source: However, in the double mutants, sla1W41AW108A and pan1∆PRD colocalize as stable patches at the cell cortex (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Most cortical patches (98.1%, 216 cortical patches from 20 cells were examined) stay nonmotile during the entire 3 min movie in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: Most cortical patches (98.1%, 216 cortical patches from 20 cells were examined) stay nonmotile during the entire 3 min movie, suggesting that endocytic internalization does not occur (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: Endocytic internalization does not occur in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: Most cortical patches (98.1%, 216 cortical patches from 20 cells were examined) stay nonmotile during the entire 3 min movie, suggesting that endocytic internalization does not occur (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of nonmotile patches.

claim: A Lucifer yellow uptake assay confirmed a severe endocytic defect in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: A Lucifer yellow uptake assay confirmed a severe endocytic defect (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on the Lucifer yellow uptake assay shown in the figure.

claim: In the double mutant cells, pan1∆PRD colocalizes with Sla2.
source: Moreover, in the double mutant cells, pan1∆PRD colocalizes with Sla2 (Figure 2F), a signature protein for endocytic sites, and the yeast homologue of vertebrate HIP1R (Engqvist-Goldstein et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: The nonmotile cortical sla1W41AW108A/pan1∆PRD patches are nonproductive endocytic sites.
source: These results indicate that the nonmotile cortical sla1W41AW108A/pan1∆PRD patches are nonproductive endocytic sites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Sla1 interacts with the yeast WASP Las17 through SH3-PRM interactions.
source: Previous in vitro studies showed that Sla1 interacts with the yeast WASP Las17 through SH3-PRM interactions (Feliciano and Di Pietro, 2012; Rodal et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In wild-type cells, Sla1 and Las17 accumulate and then leave endocytic sites with similar kinetics.
source: In wild-type cells, Sla1 and Las17 accumulate and then leave endocytic sites with similar kinetics (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: In sla1W41AW108A cells, Las17 still colocalizes with sla1W41AW108A patches.
source: In sla1W41AW108A cells, Las17 still colocalizes with sla1W41AW108A patches (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: In sla1W41AW108A cells, Las17-GFP reaches its maximum fluorescence intensity approximately 20 s after sla1W41AW108A.
source: However, Las17-GFP reaches its maximum fluorescence intensity approximately 20 s after sla1W41AW108A.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: In sla1W41AW108A cells, Las17-GFP fluorescence intensity reaches only half of its maximum value and continues to increase when sla1W41AW108A-mCherry fluorescence intensity has already begun to decline.
source: More importantly, Las17-GFP fluorescence intensity reaches only half of its maximum value and continues to increase when sla1W41AW108A-mCherry fluorescence intensity has already begun to decline.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data.

claim: In sla1W41AW108A cells, cortical recruitment of Las17 is no longer synchronized with sla1W41AW108A recruitment.
source: Thus, in sla1W41AW108A cells, cortical recruitment of Las17 is no longer synchronized with sla1W41AW108A recruitment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Sla1 plays a role in Las17 recruitment.
source: These results are consistent with a role for Sla1 in Las17 recruitment (Feliciano and Di Pietro, 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Las17 is still recruited to endocytic sites in sla1W41AW108A cells, indicating that additional proteins help to recruit Las17.
source: However, Las17 is still recruited to endocytic sites in sla1W41AW108A cells, indicating that additional proteins help to recruit Las17.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: In pan1∆PRD cells, Las17-GFP reaches its maximum fluorescence intensity about 5 s after Sla1-mCherry.
source: In pan1∆PRD cells, Las17-GFP reaches its maximum fluorescence intensity about 5 s after Sla1-mCherry (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Las17 recruitment is defective in pan1∆PRD cells, although to a lesser extent than in sla1W41AW108A cells.
source: Thus, Las17 recruitment is also defective in pan1∆PRD cells, although to a lesser extent than in sla1W41AW108A cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: In sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, cortical sla1W41AW108A patches stay non-motile at the cell cortex, while Las17 patches move dynamically along the cell cortex and throughout the cytoplasm.
source: In sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, cortical sla1W41AW108A patches stay non-motile at the cell cortex, while Las17 patches move dynamically along the cell cortex and throughout the cytoplasm (Figure 3D–F and Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures and video.

claim: Most cortical sla1W41AW108A patches did not recruit any detectable Las17 during a 2 min movie (95.4%, 131 patches from 14 cells were examined) in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: Most cortical sla1W41AW108A patches did not recruit any detectable Las17 during a 2 min movie (95.4%, 131 patches from 14 cells were examined) (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: In rare cases (4.6%), Las17 patches appeared to transiently colocalize with cortical sla1W41AW108A patches in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: In rare cases (4.6%), Las17 patches appeared to transiently colocalize with cortical sla1W41AW108A patches (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Unlike in wild-type cells, neither sla1W41AW108A patches nor Las17 patches disassemble after the transient colocalization in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: However, unlike in wild-type cells, neither sla1W41AW108A patches nor Las17 patches disassemble after the transient colocalization (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: In sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, Las17 is no longer recruited to cortical endocytic sites.
source: Thus, in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, Las17 is no longer recruited to cortical endocytic sites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: In wild-type, pan1∆PRD, or sla1W41AW108A cells, the cortical actin patch marker Abp1 appears at endocytic sites at the end of the Sla1 (or sla1 mutant) lifetime, and both proteins are internalized and disappear.
source: In wild-type, pan1∆PRD, or sla1W41AW108A cells, the cortical actin patch marker Abp1(Actin binding protein 1) appears at endocytic sites at the end of the Sla1 (or sla1 mutant) lifetime, and both proteins are internalized and disappear (Figures 4A, B and C).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: Instead of forming cortical patches in sla1 W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, actin formed comet tails.
source: Strikingly, instead of forming cortical patches in sla1 W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, actin formed comet tails, as seen with Abp1-RFP (Figure 4D) or Sac6-GFP (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: Actin comet tails slide along the cell cortex or move through the cytoplasm over time in sla1 W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: Multifocus microscopy (MFM) (Abrahamsson et al., 2013) clearly demonstrated that these actin comet tails slide along the cell cortex or move through the cytoplasm over time (Figure 4E, Video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on multifocus microscopy data shown in the figure and video.

claim: Actin comet tails do not appear to originate at or associate stably with the cortical static sla1W41AW108A patches in sla1 W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: More importantly, these actin comet tails do not appear to originate at or associate stably with the cortical static sla1W41AW108A patches in sla1 W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells (Figure 4D, Video 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure and video.

claim: Only 32 (10.5%) of 304 cortical static sla1W41AW108A patches in 30 sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells transiently colocalized with actin comet-tails during a 3 min movie.
source: We examined 304 cortical static sla1W41AW108A patches in 30 sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells and found that only 32 (10.5%) of them transiently colocalized with actin comet-tails during a 3 min movie (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: The sla1W41AW108A-GFP patches remained stationary at the cell cortex after rare, transient colocalizations with actin comet tails in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: However, unlike in wild-type cells, the sla1W41AW108A-GFP patches remained stationary at the cell cortex after these rare, transient colocalizations (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: In the sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD mutant, Las17 patches localized at the leading tips of actin comet tails and are apparently propelled by actin assembly.
source: Interestingly, in the sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD mutant, Las17 patches localized at the leading tips of actin comet tails and are apparently propelled by actin assembly in a manner similar to actin rocket tails on pathogens such as vaccinia virus or Shigella flexneri (Welch and Way, 2013) (Figure 4F, Video 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure and video, with comparison to known phenomena.

claim: Several other components of WASP-Myosin module, including Vrp1, Myo5, and Bbc1, were also observed at the leading tip of actin comet tails in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: Similar to Las17, several other components of WASP-Myosin module, including Vrp1, Myo5, and Bbc1, were also observed at the leading tip of actin comet tails in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells (Figure 4F, Video 4, and Video 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures and videos.

claim: The actin comet tails share molecular characteristics with the endocytic actin machinery.
source: These results show that the actin comet tails share molecular characteristics with the endocytic actin machinery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The endocytic actin machinery no longer assembles at cortical endocytic sites in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, but at distinct sites.
source: Thus, the endocytic actin machinery no longer assembles at cortical endocytic sites in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells, but at distinct sites, the nature of which is presently obscure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: The yeast Eps15, Ede1, is not detected at the tip of the actin comet tails in sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells.
source: Consistently, the yeast Eps15, Ede1, which is one of the early module proteins (Figure 1A) and functions in endocytic site initiation and stabilization (Kaksonen et al., 2005), is not detected at the tip of the actin comet tails (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: The WASP-Myosin module proteins can induce actin assembly and forces independent of the upstream endocytic machinery.
source: These results demonstrate that the WASP-Myosin module proteins can induce actin assembly and forces independent of the upstream endocytic machinery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented.

claim: Two Sla1 SH3 domains and the Pan1 PRD together play indispensable roles in coupling the WASP-Myosin machinery to endocytic sites.

source: Las17 NPF activity does not trigger immediate actin nucleation at endocytic sites even when we genetically disable Las17 inhibition by Sla1 in live cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: Co-existence of Vrp1 and type I myosin at endocytic sites is not sufficient to induce actin assembly until Las17 and Vrp1 levels rise to an apparent threshold level.
source: Co-existence of Vrp1 and type I myosin at endocytic sites is not sufficient to induce actin assembly until Las17 and Vrp1 levels rise to an apparent threshold level (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figure.

claim: The Las17 NPF and the Vrp1-dependent type I myosin NPF activities do not appear to be active when present at low concentrations.
source: Thus, in contrast to what was previously assumed based on in vitro studies (Feliciano and Di Pietro, 2012; Rodal et al., 2003; Sirotkin et al., 2005; Sun et al., 2006), the Las17 NPF and the Vrp1-dependent type I myosin NPF activities do not appear to be active when present at low concentrations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented, contrasting with previous in vitro studies.

claim: Multivalent PRM and SH3-domain interactions between Las17, Vrp1 and their binding partners, at endocytic sites induces formation of a higher-order complex, in which two or more VCAs are brought together to enhance affinity for the Arp2/3 complex.
source: We suggest that multivalent PRM and SH3-domain interactions between Las17, Vrp1 and their binding partners (discussed in the previous section), at endocytic sites induces formation of a higher-order complex, in which two or more VCAs are brought together to enhance affinity for the Arp2/3 complex.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data and previous literature.

claim: Las17 is part of a large and biochemically stable complex.
source: Consistently, previous studies using whole cell exacts found that Las17 is part of a large and biochemically stable complex (Feliciano and Di Pietro, 2012; Soulard et al., 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Las17 and Vrp1 accumulate at endocytic sties to a threshold level and their PRMs provide a high local concentration of multivalent interactions through which Myo3 and Myo5 are also recruited and activated in an 'all or nothing' manner.
source: In our proposed scenario, Las17 and Vrp1 accumulate at endocytic sties to a threshold level and their PRMs provide a high local concentration of multivalent interactions through which Myo3 and Myo5 are also recruited and activated in an 'all or nothing' manner.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The relationship between Las17 and Vrp1 recruitment and the switch-like onset of actin assembly observed in live cells is consistent with a mechanism based on in vitro studies in which multivalent SH3-domain and PRM interactions induce a phase transition centered around N-WASP to promote local actin assembly.
source: The relationship between Las17 and Vrp1 recruitment and the switch-like onset of actin assembly we observe in live cells is consistent with a mechanism based on in vitro studies in which multivalent SH3-domain and PRM interactions induce a phase transition centered around N-WASP to promote local actin assembly (Banjade and Rosen, 2014; Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings with previous in vitro studies.

claim: The cytoplasmic WASP-Myosin module puncta propelled by actin comet tails observed when endocytic site formation is uncoupled from actin assembly is triggered by multivalent SH3-domain and PRM interactions in the cytoplasm.
source: We speculate that the cytoplasmic WASP-Myosin module puncta propelled by actin comet tails observed when endocytic site formation is uncoupled from actin assembly (Pan1-End3 depleted cells [Sun et al., 2015] or sla1W41AW108A pan1∆PRD cells [Figure 4F]) is triggered by multivalent SH3-domain and PRM interactions in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental data and previous literature.

claim: Removing multi-PRM-containing proteins (Las17 or Vrp1) from the cytoplasm completely suppressed cytoplasmic WASP-Myosin module puncta formation and assembly of associated actin comet tails.
source: Consistently, removing multi-PRM-containing proteins (Las17 or Vrp1) from the cytoplasm, completely suppressed cytoplasmic WASP-Myosin module puncta formation and assembly of associated actin comet tails (Figure 5C–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on fluorescence microscopy data shown in the figures.

claim: Accumulation of WASP and WIP to a threshold level at endocytic sites establishes a robust, multivalent SH3 domain-PRM interaction network (possibly involving a transient phase separation), which triggers the onset of actin assembly in a switch-like manner in vivo.
source: Overall, our results strongly support a model in which accumulation of WASP and WIP to a threshold level at endocytic sites establishes a robust, multivalent SH3 domain-PRM interaction network (possibly involving a transient phase separation [Banjade and Rosen, 2014; Li et al., 2012]), which triggers the onset of actin assembly in a switch-like manner in vivo.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data and previous literature.
